messages.author: d0742ae5a689d890
messages.subject: Help with DSM analysis error
parts:
Dear Distance group,
I am working on DSM analysis of ape nests for the first time and struggling to get analysis done within the Distance software (I am still a bit uncomfortable with R).
A subset of the database is attached.

Data import seems correct to me (data structure: Study area/Region/Line transect/Segment/Observation), and I have changed survey properties so that the considered sample (and sample effort) refers to "segment" instead of "transect".
I fitted a MRDS model with single observer (hence using ds instead of ddf, right?) and used it as the analysis to obtain the detection function for DSM.
So far I have only tried very simple analysis (1 covariate max), but I keep obtaining the error:

Error in make.data(response, ddf.obj, segment.data, observation.data,  :   Effort values for segments: 32, 1268, 1554, 2259, 3217 are 0.

Effort in these lines is not 0 though (you can see it in the txt file, segment 32). I tried to delete and recreate the records, as well as deleting them completely, but the problem persists.
I am struggling to find a quick solution and your effort would be very much appreciated.  

Another error is:
Some observations are outside of detection function truncation! 

In this case, I can imagine that removing these observation would fix the problem. Removing truncation distance from the MRDS analysis worked already.

Thank you very much for your help!

Best wishes,

Mattia

messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] Help with DSM analysis error
parts:
Mattia/Group

Mattia privately shared his Distance project with me so I could run my fingers through the data to find to source of the error message.  The solution turned out to be simple, but the message that Distance generated in the Log window was deceptive.

There were indeed 5 segments in the data with an effort (length) of 0.  The problem was trying to find them.  There is a check box in Analysis | Preferences that lets you see the data as Distance begins processing it.  By checking that box (below) I could have a look at the segment-level data:

Notice the print statement at the top of the window.  Distance is printing the contents of an R data frame.  The 32nd row of that data frame contains a record with 0 Effort; one of the segments Distance was complaining about.  However, the offending segment is not the segment carrying the label 32; but instead the 32nd record in the data frame.  The data frame uses a mangled variant of the segment labels (e.g. "1. 1" and "1026. 1026") and sorts the data frame on the basis of that character representation of the segment label.

By trolling through this echo of the data, we can find that there is effort of 0 associated with segments labelled 551, 1026 (the one shown above), 2139, 2397 and 3030.  Those should be repaired and the data re-imported.

That explains the nature of the error message, but it exposes a more general issue associated with segmenting line transect data.  These 5 segments with 0 associated effort were always the last segment in a transect.  If you look through the data further, you will find, in addition to the 5 segments with 0 effort, there are 9 segments with effort (lengths) of 1m.  Segmenting of transect data by cutting transects into equal lengths with the remainder falling into the last segment can lead to arithmetic challenges of "no leftover" in some segments, and perhaps worse, very small segments always at the end of transects.  Should detections arise in those small segments, they can have a disproportional influence on the density surface modelling.

messages.author: d0742ae5a689d890
messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] Help with DSM analysis error
parts:
Dear Eric,
thank you very much for your help and very interesting insights. Indeed, the solution was easy, but the implications very relevant.

Short segments at the end of the transect is likely to be a common issue, But how could it be dealt with?
Adding these short remainders to the last previous segment would be a solution? Effort would increase only slightly.

Another aspect would be longer remainders. These should probably be imported as such, but how long should they be to be considered a valid segment?

Very interesting issue though!

Many thanks for your help and I am looking forward to how the discussion will develop.

Best wishes,

Mattia

messages.author: f2122b34f1aa6e95
messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] Help with DSM analysis error
parts:
Mattia

There is no universal answer to the question of "what is the proper segment length".  One rule of thumb is for segments to be twice the truncation distance (making the 2-dimensional shape of a segment roughly square).  Another rule of thumb is for segments to all be roughly equal in length (your segments differ in length by two orders of magnitude (1 to 100).
